subject: Re: MAP: Technical evaluation plan — benchmark targets & shortlist
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Olson <jared.olson@acme-retail.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: MAP: Technical evaluation plan — next steps

Hi Jared / Priya —

Great to meet you both earlier. As discussed, attached is the draft MAP focused on the Technical Evaluation milestone. High-level recap and proposed next steps: 

1) Benchmark success criteria (owner: Acme / SE support)
   - 95th percentile generation latency <= 450ms for typical 256-token requests (measured end-to-end from Acme client to Redwood hosted endpoint)
   - Median token cost target <= $0.0007/token for the peak query mix (we'll validate with our cost model)
   - Quality: top-1 accuracy on your canonical NLU benchmark >= 88% (see attached benchmark-specs.csv for dataset splits)

2) Model shortlist (Redwood to provision):
   - redwood/longform-v2-7b-quant 
   - open/opt-13b-int8 (baseline)
   - community/gpt-like-13b-qlora (fast path for latency)

3) Test plan & responsibilities:
   - Acme: provide 1K representative prompts + ground-truth labels for the quality eval (Priya to share) — due 12/08
   - Redwood (Camila / Mateo): run latency + cost benchmarks, produce per-model report — target 12/11
   - Joint: review results, pick preferred model and quantization profile — meeting 12/13

4) Dependencies / blockers:
   - Need VPN access or allowlist for Acme test CIDR (security) — Acme action
   - Confirm acceptable data retention window for logs used in benchmarking (security/compliance)

I've attached a lighter MAP draft (acme-map-draft-v2.docx) and the benchmark spec template (benchmark-specs.csv). Please reply with any edits to the success criteria or timeline.

Thanks — looking forward to the run.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
[Attachment: acme-map-draft-v2.docx]

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jared Olson <jared.olson@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme-retail.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Dec 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP: Technical evaluation plan — next steps

Thanks Marissa — quick notes from the SE side: 

- Latency measurement: we'll provide both end-to-end and server-side (Redwood) numbers. For E2E we'll instrument from an Acme VM; if VPN is slower than expected we can also run from an Acme dev region to approximate production.
- Cost model: attached latency-cost-targets.xlsx includes per-model per-token cost estimates with our current quantization profiles. Expect the int8/qlora variants to be 20-35% cheaper than fp16.
- Model shortlist: I recommend we include a small LLM-8k-context variant for your long-form assistant tests (I added redwood/longform-v2-7b-8k to the notes).

Action items I picked up:
- I will spin up the benchmark harness and share a load script + instructions by 12/09.
- Mateo will run initial throughput tests once we have the sample prompts.

I'll attach the harness README and the run template in a follow-up.

Camila
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: latency-cost-targets.xlsx]

From: Jared Olson <jared.olson@acme-retail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme-retail.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Dec 2026 11:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP: Technical evaluation plan — next steps

Thanks Marissa / Camila — couple clarifying Qs from my side: 

1) For the 95th percentile latency target, are you measuring from Acme client SDK to Redwood hosted endpoint (including network + proxy) or from Redwood ingress to model? We'd prefer the latter for repeatability.
2) For the quality metric: can you confirm the evaluation harness supports our intent taxonomy (12 intents) and the slot-filling F1? We'll push the sample dataset today.

Also, on security: our infra team needs a one-pager describing what logs Redwood retains during benchmarking and who has access. Priya, looping you for procurement/security coordination.

-Jared
Director of AI Platforms, Acme Retail

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Olson <jared.olson@acme-retail.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Dec 2026 09:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP: Technical evaluation plan — next steps

Thanks for the questions, Jared — quick responses and updated owners/timelines below.

1) Latency measurement: Camila confirms we'll provide both metrics. For the MAP success criterion we'll publish the Redwood-ingress-only numbers (to be fully repeatable) and include an E2E note in the report.

2) Quality eval: Camila / Mateo will adapt the harness to compute intent accuracy + slot F1. Please drop the CSV (1K prompts) into the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/abc123 by COB 12/08.

Security one-pager: attaching a short doc (in thread) that summarizes retention and access controls for benchmark logs. Priya — please confirm this satisfies your infra team's request or call out any gaps.

Updated milestones (MAP technical evaluation):
- 12/08: Acme uploads labeled eval set (owner: Acme — Priya)
- 12/09: Redwood shares benchmark harness + run instructions (owner: Camila)
- 12/11: Redwood delivers model-level latency/cost/quality report (owner: Mateo)
- 12/13: Joint review + model selection (owners: Marissa / Jared)
- Target close date for this MAP milestone: 12/20/2026

If those dates look good I will update the MAP doc and send an updated DocuSign link for the PO (related_links).

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: benchmark-logs-retention-one-pager.pdf]
